look_here_first: Examine stem and node hairs with magnification: O. stricta often shows spreading hairs, including SEPTATE hairs at nodes, rather than the densely straight, forward-appressed NONSEPTATE hairs of O. dillenii. Check flower-cluster size and mature capsules only as supporting traits.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Herbaceous woodsorrel with upright to spreading leafy stems; habit overlaps O. dillenii and can be altered by mowing.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Trifoliolate with notched, heartlike leaflets; leaf outline alone does not distinguish similar yellow Oxalis.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Hairs often spreading, with a mix of septate and nonseptate hairs; septate hairs particularly informative at stem nodes.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Yellow five-petaled flowers, often several per inflorescence (frequently 5–7); petals typically 8–11 mm but variable.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Slender capsule commonly 8–15 mm; fruit length alone is not decisive.
